lessons.title: Persistent Client-Side Storage with localStorage
lessons.description: Store data in the browser that persists even after the page is closed and reopened.

sections.heading: What is localStorage?
paragraphs: localStorage lets you store key-value pairs in the browser. The data persists indefinitely — it survives page refreshes, browser restarts and even computer restarts until explicitly deleted.
list: Stores only strings — numbers and objects must be serialized
Capacity: about 5–10 MB depending on the browser
Synchronous API — blocks the main thread during reads/writes
Scoped to the origin (protocol + domain + port)

sections.heading: Basic operations
list: localStorage.key(index) — get the key at a specific index

codeExamples.heading: Basic localStorage operations
explanation: All values are stored as strings — even numbers.
getItem returns null if the key doesn't exist.
clear() removes everything — use removeItem for selective deletion.

practice.task: Store your name in localStorage, then retrieve it and display it on the page. Close the browser, reopen the page, and verify the data is still there.

keyTakeaways: localStorage persists data across browser sessions — it never expires automatically.
All values are stored as strings — use JSON.stringify() and JSON.parse() for objects.
Data is scoped to the current origin (domain + port + protocol).
Use removeItem() or clear() to manage stored data.
lessons.challenge: Build a "last visited" timestamp that shows when the user last loaded the page, then updates the timestamp for the next visit.

lessons.title: Session-Scoped Storage with sessionStorage
lessons.description: Store data that lasts only for the current browser tab — closed when the tab closes.

sections.heading: sessionStorage vs localStorage
paragraphs: sessionStorage works exactly like localStorage but with one key difference: data is cleared when the browser tab or window is closed. It's perfect for temporary state like form progress or wizard steps.
list: Data is cleared when the tab/window closes
Each tab has its own independent sessionStorage

codeExamples.heading: Using sessionStorage
explanation: sessionStorage behaves identically to localStorage with one exception: tab lifecycle.
Each browser tab maintains its own independent sessionStorage.
Data is cleared automatically when the tab closes.
Perfect for temporary, per-session data like multi-step forms.

practice.task: Create a multi-step form where each step's data is stored in sessionStorage. When the user returns to the page in the same tab, restore their progress.
hints: On page load, check sessionStorage.getItem("step") to restore.

keyTakeaways: sessionStorage has the same API as localStorage but data is tab-scoped and temporary.
Data is cleared when the tab or window closes.
Each tab has its own independent sessionStorage — they don't share data.
Use sessionStorage for temporary per-session state like form progress.
lessons.challenge: Build a form wizard with 3 steps. Save the current step in sessionStorage so refreshing the page restores the user's position.

lessons.title: Persisting Complex Objects using JSON Serialization
lessons.description: Store arrays and objects in localStorage by converting them to JSON strings and back.

sections.heading: The serialization problem
paragraphs: localStorage only stores strings. To save arrays, objects or other complex data, you must serialize them to JSON strings with JSON.stringify() and deserialize them back with JSON.parse().
list: JSON.stringify(object) — converts an object to a JSON string
JSON.parse(string) — converts a JSON string back to an object
Always wrap parse in try/catch — corrupted data throws errors
This is the standard pattern for persisting complex data in localStorage

codeExamples.heading: Storing and retrieving objects
explanation: JSON.stringify() converts the array into a string for storage.
JSON.parse() converts it back into a usable JavaScript array.
Always use try/catch around JSON.parse() — corrupted data will crash your app.
This pattern works for any JavaScript value: objects, arrays, nested structures.

practice.task: Create a simple counter app that saves the count to localStorage using JSON.stringify. When the page loads, retrieve and display the saved count.
hints: The || 0 handles the case where nothing is stored yet.

keyTakeaways: localStorage stores only strings — use JSON.stringify() to save objects.
Use JSON.parse() to retrieve objects — always wrap in try/catch.
The || defaultValue pattern handles the first-visit case gracefully.
This JSON serialize/deserialize pattern is the foundation of client-side data persistence.
lessons.challenge: Build a bookmark manager that stores an array of bookmark objects (title, url, date) in localStorage. Add, remove and display bookmarks, persisting them between sessions.
